# Responsible AI, applied.

I'm Adam M. Słociński, principal of Balans, an independent data and AI engineering practice. I help organizations use AI on the data they already have, and help fill out the required paperwork too.  

I like libraries, cheering for the underdogs, and computers that work in airplane mode.

## Who this is for

I build local, in-process, on-device solutions that keep your data private and under your control, designed to meet regulatory compliance. Think WCAG 2.2 accessibility targets; alignment with FAIR principles; submitting an algorithmic assessment impact; or one-pager on your exposure to the EU AI Act; all the while without vendor lock-in or long-term contracts. 

If you sell or deploy AI into the EU, and the AI Act's high-risk rules apply to you, or you manage a public or cultural institution, and want to learn how AI can make your archives and records digital and queryable, contact me.

## What I can deliver

### EU AI Act readiness
The Exposure Inventory lists every AI system you deploy or sell into the EU and what the Act requires of each:
your exposure on one page. The Classification Memo takes a given system and states, with reasoning,
whether it is high-risk and what that sets off; it is written to hand to counsel. The AI Literacy Program (Article
4) trains your staff on your own systems, not on generic slides. Where the Act calls for a Fundamental Rights
Impact Assessment, I draft the working file behind it.

### Records and documents-AI pilots and more

A small working system built over documents you already hold (case files, catalogues, reports,
correspondence), answering the questions you choose. You keep the code, the documentation, and the
training. The pilot produces its own paper trail, inventory and classification and documentation, which is why
the governance advice and the build can come from the same desk

## How I work

Embedded, scoped, handed over. I work embedded with your team, within your constraints, until the
deliverable is complete and handed over. After that, you decide whether to extend the engagement or close it.
Local-first is what makes the advice practical: what I recommend are systems I have built, private and
auditable, on infrastructure you control, with no third-party cloud routing unless you choose it. Standards are a
standing habit, not an add-on. WCAG 2.2 AA (AAA criteria where feasible) and FAIR data principles, in every
deliverable. Every engagement is project-based, with a defined scope and a defined end date, and code,
documentation, and training included. Prices are quoted per project after scoping, and the scoping report is
yours to use however you choose.

## About the name

Several cultures share the idea of something being “just right” (not too much, not too little). Like the Earth’s axial tilt, a small but well-placed adjustment can be what makes everything feel optimized and well-balanced. That’s the standard I hold myself to.
